documents.unit: AI Steering Council / AI Task Force
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Acceptable Use Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy sets shared duties (data, ethics, integrity) but says 'Instructors should include a policy in all their syllabi' and notes 'disciplinary differences', handing the AI-use decision to instructors.
documents.summary: University-wide acceptable use policy (Aug 2025) covering teaching, research and administration. It defines AI, sets data and legal duties, asks instructors to write a syllabus policy and routes violations to existing misconduct procedures.

units.why: The purpose clause says the policy exists for 'safeguarding academic integrity, data privacy, and institutional values', which is an institution-level statement of purpose and principles, so P56 fits.
units.anchor: safeguarding academic integrity, data privacy, and institutional values

units.why: States the policy 'will be revisited and updated as AI evolves', a provisional-policy statement matching P54.
units.anchor: This policy will be revisited and updated as AI evolves.

units.why: The scope clause sets who the policy binds ('all members of the Brandeis community'), which is a scope statement under the institution-wide framework type P56.
units.anchor: applies to all members of the Brandeis community, including students, faculty, staff, and affiliates

units.why: Defines 'Artificial Intelligence (AI)', setting what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: Computer systems designed to do tasks that usually require human intelligence.

units.why: Defines 'Generative AI' as a subset that creates 'text, images, music, or code', a scope-setting definition, P61.
units.anchor: subset of AI designed to create new content, such as text, images, music, or code

units.why: Defines 'Machine Learning AI' to delimit what the policy covers, P61.
units.anchor: of AI that focuses on learning from existing data without the generation of new content.

units.why: 'All AI applications must comply with' data governance and cybersecurity policies: a mandatory data-protection rule, P50 (data handling rather than tool vetting).
units.anchor: All AI applications must comply with Brandeis' data governance protocols and cybersecurity policies.

units.why: 'Use of regulated, restricted, or confidential information in AI tools requires appropriate authorization and safeguards' limits what data goes into AI, so P50.
units.anchor: Use of regulated, restricted, or confidential information in AI tools requires appropriate authorization and safeguards.

units.why: Members 'must ensure that AI tools are used ethically, maintaining the integrity and originality of their work', which makes submitted work the person's own, so P29 over P53 (no harms named).
units.anchor: ensure that AI tools are used ethically, maintaining the integrity and originality of their work

units.why: Requires members to 'adhere to applicable laws' including intellectual property law; P52 chosen as the legal/IP type since the rule also names FERPA and other laws.
units.anchor: must adhere to applicable laws and legal obligations when using AI

units.why: Requires compliance with 'contracts, end user agreements, and other terms' of AI tools, i.e. terms of use, P52.
units.anchor: must comply with applicable contracts, end user agreements, and other terms

units.why: 'Instructors should include a policy in all their syllabi' on generative AI use and misuse is a syllabus-statement requirement, P09.
units.anchor: include a policy in all their syllabi regarding the use (and misuse) of generative AI

units.why: Instructors should 'dedicate some time in class discussing the reasons for how AI can be used', i.e. communicating expectations; P09 is the closest communicate-type.
units.anchor: dedicate some time in class discussing the reasons for how AI can be used

units.why: States there 'will be disciplinary differences in how AI is integrated into coursework', leaving the rule to be set per course/discipline, P04.
units.anchor: will be disciplinary differences in how AI is integrated into coursework depending on learning objectives

units.why: 'Students are expected to maintain the University's standards of academic integrity, including the use of artificial intelligence' puts AI use under integrity rules, P36 (nearest enforcement/integrity type).
units.anchor: maintain the University’s standards of academic integrity, including the use of artificial intelligence

units.why: Research AI content 'should be critically evaluated and not solely relied upon', a verify-output rule; P31 rather than P62 because the rule is about checking output.
units.anchor: AI-generated content should be critically evaluated and not solely relied upon for research conclusions.

units.why: Researchers are 'encouraged to ensure that AI tools are used ethically' with integrity and originality of their work.
units.anchor: Researchers are encouraged to ensure that AI tools are used ethically

units.why: 'Regulated, restricted, and confidential data should never be input into AI tools without proper safeguards and approvals' is a data-protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: should never be input into AI tools without proper safeguards and approvals

units.why: 'The author, not the technology, is accountable' for mistakes AI makes with preprints or data sets, so authors own what they publish, P29.
units.anchor: the author, not the technology, is accountable

units.why: Researchers using AI in human subjects research 'must consult with' the HRPP, a research-governance rule deferring to an IRB-type body, P62.
units.anchor: must consult with the

units.why: AI use in publications and grant proposals 'may be restricted by publisher and funder policies', deferring to venue and funder rules, P62.
units.anchor: may be restricted by publisher and funder policies
units.frag_start: The use of AI in preparing

units.why: Staff are 'encouraged to explore AI tools to enhance efficiency in administrative tasks'; this is administrative, non-teaching AI use that no type covers, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Staff are also encouraged to explore
units.policy: Staff are also encouraged to explore AI tools to enhance efficiency in administrative tasks
units.uncovered_note: Staff use of AI for administrative work (data analysis, scheduling, communication), outside teaching and research.

units.why: 'Employees are required to use University-approved and provided AI tools if using University data' pushes use of vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Employees are required to use University-approved and provided AI tools if using University data

units.why: Employees may 'make requests for new tools' through ITAC or ATAC, a tool-review route, P65.
units.anchor: make requests for new tools through the
units.policy: Employees may make requests for new AI tools through the IT Advisory Committee (ITAC) for operational and administrative AI technologies or the Academic Technology Advisory Committee (ATAC) for academic-use and research AI technologies.

units.why: Departments 'must follow the university's procurement policies and obtain necessary approvals' from ATAC or ITAC before acquiring AI tools, institutional review of AI acquisition, P65.
units.anchor: must follow the university's procurement policies and obtain necessary approvals

units.why: 'Violations of this policy will be addressed in accordance with existing university procedures for academic and administrative misconduct' treats violations as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be addressed in accordance with existing university procedures

units.why: 'The AI Task Force will periodically review and update this policy' is a review-cycle commitment, P54.
units.anchor: The AI Task Force will periodically review and update this policy

units.why: Directs people to the CTL 'for guidance on AI use in teaching and learning', a support resource for instructors, P63.
units.anchor: contact the Center for Teaching and Learning (CTL)

documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The page tells instructors to include a policy and offers four templates 'ranging from more restrictive to more permissive' for faculty to adopt or modify, so it sets no stance itself.
tiers: Policy B1 (situational; permitted for background learning)
Policy B2 (situational; permitted for refining assignments)
documents.summary: CTL guide requiring a syllabus AI statement and supplying four template policies from full ban to open use with citation. Instructors adopt, modify or write their own.

units.anchor: Instructors should include a policy in each of their course syllabi

units.why: Advises to 'review the policy carefully with your students and to have regular conversations in class', especially before major assignments; communicating expectations, P09.

units.why: The university 'offers four policy templates ranging from more restrictive to more permissive': named levels of AI use, P05.
units.anchor: ranging from more restrictive to more permissive

units.anchor: adopt one of the template statements as-is;

units.anchor: one of the template statements to more closely align with the circumstances of their course

documents.title: AI Tools at Brandeis
documents.stance_why: The page lists tools the university provides ('Brandeis provides Gen AI tools with data protection') without restricting or requiring their use; the university supports use of vetted tools.
documents.summary: Lists the Gen AI tools Brandeis licenses (Gemini, NotebookLM, Copilot, Zoom AI), notes data protection, and describes how new products are requested and reviewed.

units.why: 'Brandeis provides Gen AI tools with data protection to students, faculty, and staff' means the university supplies sanctioned tools, P17.
units.anchor: Brandeis provides Gen AI tools with data protection to students, faculty, and staff.

units.why: 'Your chat prompts are not used to train the underlying large language models' with Brandeis credentials: a data-protection fact, P50.
units.anchor: your chat prompts are not used to train the underlying large language models

units.why: 'Other tools may not offer this kind of data protection' warns users and favors vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Other tools may not offer this kind of data protection.

units.why: 'Please be aware of all Brandeis Data Governance policies to ensure the safety and proper use of university data', P50.
units.anchor: Please be aware of all Brandeis Data Governance policies

units.anchor: will continue to assess requests for new AI products and services as they come in

notes: brandeis-students (AI Framework for Brandeis Students) was screened include, but the saved text contains only site navigation and an 'Accessible PDF' link; the five-question framework body was not captured, so it has no codable units and is omitted from documents.
